summary:
The doom3 build is correct and ready. Two of the builder's claims about multiplayer were wrong, and I fixed them in place.

**What was built.** base/zz_fleetvideo.pk4 for DOOM 3 1.3: 69,371 B, md5 9608103a37eb82327c49b35905431f48. Three rebuilds were byte-identical. It holds copies of pak007's guis/mainmenu.gui and guis/mpmain.gui. In each copy only the two Screen Size lines change:
- choices becomes the exact text of #str_04222 plus ";Native";
- values becomes "3;4;5;6;7;8;-1".

**Checked independently of the builder's script:**
- A byte diff against the staged pak007 (md5 6319f086...) shows one changed region per file, exactly the anchor lines at 0x1c765/0x1c799 and 0x19316/0x19331. mainmenu keeps LF line endings and mpmain keeps CRLF.
- These two GUIs are the only files in any base or d3xp pk4 that mention r_mode, and pak007 is the last pak to ship each of them.

**Engine behaviour, read in id's GPL source rather than recalled:**
- Pk4s are sorted case-insensitively and each is placed right after its directory, so zz_ wins.
- The choices string is translated as one whole token when the GUI is parsed, so the literal list is split up exactly as #str_04222 is.
- The values parser turns "-" "1" into "-1". The menu then matches the cvar's string, so r_mode -1 now shows "Native". The stock menu showed its first entry, "640x480".

**Main correction.** The pk4 contains only .gui files, which id's pure-server rules ignore. That makes it "PURE_NEVER", and the 1.3 exe carries the same exclusion table. Such a pk4 is never put on a pure server's required list, and a client keeps using it even while connected to a pure server. So two builder statements were wrong:
- "a client-only pk4 is excluded on a pure server";
- "--install-server keeps a future pure server's list containing the fix".

This matters in practice. "Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat" starts a listen server without setting si_pure, which defaults to 1, so every fleet LAN game is a pure server. If the pk4 held even one non-GUI file (a readme.txt would do it), the host would put the pk4 on its required list, because mpmain.gui is read when the map loads. Every box without the identical pk4 would then be refused. --build now refuses such a pk4.

**Other fixes to apply.py:**
- --check now prints the engine-mirrored menu selection and verifies #str_04222 against the staged strings/english.lang.
- --check also verifies that both launchers still pass r_mode -1 and r_customWidth/Height.
- --install-server is now a documented no-op for this pk4.
- --publish --dry-run no longer prints "published".

Tests went from 15 to 28, all passing. Nothing was published, and no box, server or service was touched.
launcher_changes_needed: None required. Play DOOM 3.bat and Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat already pass `+set r_mode -1 +set r_customWidth %FR_W% +set r_customHeight %FR_H% +set r_aspectRatio %FR_D3AR%`, which is exactly what the 'Native' entry selects. apply.py --check now fails if either launcher stops passing the first three.

Do NOT add `+set si_pure 0` to Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat for this patch. Every fleet LAN game stays pure (si_pure defaults to 1), and the GUI-only pk4 is unaffected: it is never on a pure list, and a box without it can still join.

No GAMERES or FLEETRES change. DOOM 3 stays command-line-only and no cfg is written, so there is nothing for the two writers to disagree about and no generated value contains parentheses. The pk4 is a new file inside the title tree, so GAMESYNC ships it. Boxes that are already provisioned need GAMESYNC RESET + START, or a purge + resync, to receive it.

No server install. ~/doom3-server runs `+set si_pure 0` (the running entry.sh is identical to the repo copy), and the pk4 would not be required even if the server were pure. `apply.py --install-server` now reports NOT NEEDED and copies nothing.
risks: The pk4 must stay GUI-only. Any non-excluded member, even a readme.txt, makes it PURE_NEUTRAL. Every fleet LAN game is a pure listen server and reads mpmain.gui at map load, so the pk4 would then land on the host's required list and lock out every box without the identical pk4. --build refuses this and a test pins it. Anyone editing apply.py later must keep it that way.

Hardware has not yet shown the menu's 'Native' entry. The support is strong: GPL ChoiceWindow parses negative values and matches the cvar string, the stock invert-mouse control ships values "0.022;-0.022", and the retail exe carries the ChoiceWindow warning string. The hardware plan is what proves it.
The Screen Size labels are now a literal English list, so they no longer follow the game's language setting. The fleet runs English only.

The pk4 carries full copies of two stock GUIs (about 700 KB and 140 KB unpacked), which would hide any newer official copy. --check fails if pak007 stops being the effective stock owner of either file.

Only the base game is covered. If Resurrection of Evil content is ever staged, d3xp/pak001.pk4's own mainmenu/mpmain would win under fs_game d3xp, and the pk4 would need a d3xp twin. It is inert today because RoE is not installed.

First launch on a box that has never run DOOM 3 (.145 today). id's first-run hardware detection (Common.cpp Com_ExecMachineSpec_f) sets r_mode to 3, 4 or 5 after init. With a valid CD key, AddStartupCommands re-runs the command line's `set r_mode -1` straight afterwards. If the key check fails, or R_InitOpenGL falls back to safe mode, that session stays on 3/4/5 and the control shows that mode. This is not a pk4 fault; relaunch once.

DoomConfig.cfg is only rewritten when an archived cvar changed during the session (Common.cpp WriteConfiguration). So .123's stale `seta r_mode "3"` survives a plain launch-and-quit. That is harmless, because the launcher re-applies r_mode -1 at every start, but it makes DoomConfig.cfg a misleading check unless the menu changed r_mode.
On .145, DISPLAYCFG get reads the inactive Intel HD adapter (CLAUDE.md), so it cannot confirm 1920x1080 there. Use the screenshot size or the game console instead.

The HUD and menus are 640x480 virtual and stretch at 16:9. This is cosmetic and the patch does not change it. There is still no in-menu aspect control, because the Video box has no free row (rows at y 125/150/175, warning at 205, verified). The launcher sets r_aspectRatio per box at every start.
Rollout: the pk4 only reaches boxes that are GAMESYNCed with RESET + START, or purged and resynced. .240 still holds Doom3 even though the gate now refuses it there for disk space.
hw_verification_plan:
**Before testing (future publish phase)**
- Run `apply.py --check`, then `--build`, then `--publish`.
- Run `python3 scripts/validate-staged-library.py --quiet`.
- On the first test box, purge C:\Games\Doom3 and its .lnk, then GAMESYNC RESET + START.
- Accept the sync only if: state=done, failed_files 0, titles_done == titles_total, and titles_total equals the library's count for that box.
- DIRLIST must show C:\Games\Doom3\base\zz_fleetvideo.pk4 at 69,371 B (md5 9608103a37eb82327c49b35905431f48).

**Box order**
- .123 first: XP, has run Doom 3, and SCREENSHOT 0 captures fullscreen GL there.
- .145 next: it has never launched Doom 3, so launch once and quit cleanly before the real test.
- Then .240.
- .195 last: Windows 7, where GDI cannot capture exclusive fullscreen, so rely on the console and condump.

**Launch**
- `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Doom3" "Play DOOM 3.bat"`.
- Judge the resolution by the SCREENSHOT 0 size on XP (1920x1080) or by the console.
- Do not use DISPLAYCFG get on .145: it reads the inactive Intel HD adapter.

**Engine proof (keyboard only)**
1. Open the console with Ctrl+Alt+~.
2. Run `path`. The line ending base\zz_fleetvideo.pk4 (2 files) must appear ABOVE the pak007.pk4 (38 files) line. This proves precedence on the box.
3. Query:
   - `r_mode` must be -1. If a first-ever launch shows 3/4/5, that is id's first-run hardware detection, not the pk4 (see risks); relaunch.
   - `r_customWidth` and `r_customHeight` must be 1920 and 1080 on the LCDs.
   - `r_aspectRatio` must be 1.
4. Run `condump fleetres_check.txt`, DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Doom3\base\fleetres_check.txt, then DELETE it.

**Menu proof (plan for a person)**
The menu cursor follows relative mouse movement. One CLICKSHOT on the Screen Size control can test absolute clicks, but expect it to fail.
- Main menu > Settings > System > Video: 'Screen Size' must read **Native**. The stock menu shows 640x480 there.
- Cycle the control: 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x1024, 1600x1200, then Native.
- Pick 1600x1200 and Apply. The game must switch; confirm by screenshot size or console.
- Pick Native and Apply. It must return to 1920x1080.
- Screenshot each state.
- Quit cleanly after that session, DOWNLOAD base\DoomConfig.cfg, and check for `seta r_mode "-1"`. The config is only rewritten when an archived cvar changed, so a plain launch-and-quit leaving .123's old "3" is not a failure.

**Pure LAN proof (do this before the pk4 reaches the second box)**
1. Box A, patched, runs 'DOOM 3 - Host LAN Game'. That is a pure listen server, because si_pure defaults to 1.
2. Box B, still without zz_fleetvideo.pk4, joins. It MUST join. Screenshot both boxes, with both players in the game.
3. On A's console after the map loads, `path` must print `not on the pure list` under zz_fleetvideo.pk4.
4. Then give B the pk4 and rejoin. On B, ESC > System > Screen Size must show Native even though it is connected to a pure server. B's `path` must also say `not on the pure list`.
5. Finally join the fleet dedicated server at 192.168.1.132:27666 (si_pure 0) from a patched box.

**What must NOT change**
- Single-player starts as before.
- Fullscreen, Brightness and the Audio rows behave exactly as stock.
- LAN hosting and joining work as above, including with a mix of patched and unpatched boxes.
- The desktop returns to its proper mode after the game quits.
review_notes:
**Verified independently of the builder's script**
- **Staged original.** pak007.pk4 md5 6319f086f930ec1618ab09b4c20c268c, 192,031 B.
  - The member sizes, CRCs and md5s match: mainmenu e90e5f71..., mpmain c7adb074....
  - All four anchor lines and byte offsets match (0x1c765, 0x1c799, 0x19316, 0x19331). mainmenu uses LF only; mpmain uses CRLF throughout.
  - #str_04222 in pak007's strings/english.lang is exactly "640x480;800x600;1024x768;1152x864;1280x1024;1600x1200".
  - The stock GUI already uses the patterns the builder relies on: invert-mouse on m_pitch with values "0.022;-0.022", and literal lists "No;Yes" and "best;oss;alsa".
  - Across every base and d3xp pk4, only guis/mainmenu.gui and guis/mpmain.gui mention r_mode. pak007 is the last pak shipping each: mainmenu comes from pak000/005/006/007, mpmain from pak000/005/007.
- **Built output.** A prefix/suffix byte diff shows one changed region per GUI, and it is exactly the two anchor lines. Line counts are equal and the line endings are kept.
  - The zip has two deflate members, flags 0, no extras and no data descriptors, and testzip passes.
  - Three rebuilds were byte-identical, and they match the builder's file.
- **Engine behaviour, from id's GPL source (neo/, fetched into the scratchpad):**
  - Precedence: AddGameDirectory inserts each pak right after its directory, after idStrList::Sort, whose comparator is the case-insensitive idStr::Icmp. Later names win.
  - "choices" is a registered STRING var translated as one whole token when parsed (RegExp.cpp AddReg), so the literal is split up exactly as #str_04222 is.
  - The values parser has a negNum branch that makes "-1", and UpdateChoice's string match then selects Native.
  - r_mode has no min/max, and R_GetModeInfo(-1) uses r_customWidth/Height.
  - pureExclusions and GetPackStatus make a GUI-only pk4 PURE_NEVER. UpdatePureServerChecksums skips it, and the pure-mode file filter keeps it.
  - si_pure defaults to "1". idMultiplayerGame::Reset reads mpmain.gui at map load. WriteConfiguration and first-run hardware detection behave as described in the risks.
- **Retail 1.3 DOOM3.exe** (md5 7cd77c22...) carries the same exclusion strings together in .rdata (".pda" ".gui" ".pd" "sound/VO"), the path and pure-list console strings, and the ChoiceWindow warning.
- **Launchers and server.**
  - Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat uses +spawnServer and sets no si_pure, so it runs a PURE listen server. The builder did not consider this.
  - ~/doom3-server runs si_pure 0, and its running entry.sh is identical to the repo copy.
- **--publish** matches sharewrite.py's interface: `put <local> <dest relative to the share>` with `--dry-run`, and sharewrite verifies the md5 through /mnt and checks for a fresh mtime. The flow backs up before replacing, handles one file, stops on the first failure, is idempotent, and is proven by a stubbed test. It was not run.
- **Nothing written anywhere it shouldn't be.** The share has no zz_ file and no _patches/Doom3, and ~/doom3-server is unchanged. The worktree holds no game data: only apply.py, the 2-hunk .diff and the test.
  - The builder's `__pycache__` was gitignored; I removed it anyway.
  - The committed .diff shows mpmain's hunk with CRs stripped. It is only a readable description: apply.py regenerates from byte anchors, and the output keeps CRLF, which I verified.

**Changed** (only in provisioning/patches/doom3/apply.py and tests/python/test_patch_doom3.py, plus review evidence)
- **apply.py:**
  - Added id's pure rules (pure_excluded, pak_pure_status, searched_on_pure_server, enters_pure_list), with a build gate `require_pure_never` and a `pure_status` field in the manifest.
  - Added a ChoiceWindow value mirror (engine_values, engine_current_choice). --check now asserts that r_mode -1 selects Native, where the stock menu showed 640x480.
  - --check verifies #str_04222 from english.lang and checks both launchers' r_mode -1 / r_customWidth / r_customHeight premise, looking the files up case-insensitively.
  - --install-server was a copy with restart advice and a wrong rationale. It is now a documented no-op for a PURE_NEVER pk4.
  - --publish --dry-run no longer prints "published".
  - The docstring now cites the source code rather than memory.
- **Tests:** 13 added (28 total).

**Report corrections**
- The two wrong pure-server statements are replaced.
- The precedence rule is now source-verified.
- The hardware plan gained:
  - `path` as proof of precedence and of pure-list status;
  - the mixed patched/unpatched pure LAN test;
  - the .145 DISPLAYCFG caveat;
  - the first-run and DoomConfig caveats.

**Kept the builder's choices**
- Also patching mpmain.gui: correct, since it is the multiplayer ESC menu.
- Dropping the aspect row: the layout claim was verified.
- The "Native" label: FLEETRES sets r_customWidth/Height per box, so no fixed number would be right everywhere.
